stories.title: Sky Harbour Secures Approvals for Two Ground Leases at Van Nuys Airport
stories.excerpt: Sky Harbour Group Corporation, an aviation infrastructure company building a nationwide network of Home Base Operator (HBO) campuses for business aircraft, announced that the Los Angeles City Council has approved two ground leases at Van Nuys Airport for the development of Sky Harbour HBO campuses. The ground leases, which will yield a total of 10 aircraft hangars, are expected to be formally executed in the coming weeks. Van Nuys Airport is one of the most active general aviation airports in the country and is the primary business aviation gateway to Los Angeles. “Van Nuys operators have actively been seeking the Sky Harbour Home Base Operator model, and we are excited to deliver it,” said Tal Keinan, CEO of Sky Harbour. “We are grateful to the Los Angeles City Council, the Board of Airport Commissioners and to the Van Nuys and Los Angeles World Airports teams for their partnership. Sky Harbour plans to bring new and lasting value to the airport, to Los Angeles Business Aviation, and to the San Fernando Valley community.” The post Sky Harbour Secures Approvals for Two Ground Leases at Van Nuys Airport appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Sky Harbour Group secures LA City Council approval for two ground leases at Van Nuys Airport.
Project will yield 10 aircraft hangars supporting business aviation infrastructure.
Van Nuys is primary business aviation gateway to Los Angeles, one of most active general aviation airports.
stories.summary: Sky Harbour Group Corporation received Los Angeles City Council approval for two ground leases at Van Nuys Airport to develop Home Base Operator (HBO) campuses, totaling 10 aircraft hangars. Van Nuys Airport is the primary business aviation gateway to Los Angeles and one of the most active general aviation airports in the country. Ground leases are expected to be formally executed in coming weeks.
stories.impact: Minimal direct relevance to multifamily development. Aviation infrastructure expansion signals broader commercial/industrial activity in San Fernando Valley and greater Los Angeles, which could support ancillary demand for workforce housing near airport employment clusters, but this is indirect and secondary.

stories.title: White Plains Project is First to Break Ground on NY State’s Housing Acceleration Fund
stories.excerpt: Construction has begun on North White Plains, a $178-million mixed-income, transit-oriented development that will create 296 new apartments in the city of White Plains. The development, which will feature two six-story buildings, retail space and a publicly accessible park, is the first development to utilize Gov. Kathy Hochul’s Housing Acceleration Fund, a program designed to jumpstart construction of shovel-ready mixed-income housing projects across New York State. Financing for the development, which closed this past July, includes approximately $120.6 million in construction financing from Merchants Capital, a $10-million loan from The Community Preservation Corporation, $18 million in financing from New York State Homes and Community Renewal and approximately $29.7 million in equity from developers Basis Investment Group and BRP Companies. Thirty of the complex’s 296 units will be designated as affordable housing. Completion of North White Plains is anticipated for the second quarter of 2029. bullets: North White Plains breaks ground: $178M, 296-unit transit-oriented development, two six-story buildings.
First project funded via NY State Housing Acceleration Fund; 30 units designated affordable.
Financing: $120.6M construction (Merchants Capital), $10M CPC, $18M state, $29.7M equity; completion Q2 2029.
stories.summary: North White Plains, a $178 million mixed-income, transit-oriented development with 296 apartments, began construction in Westchester County and is the first project to utilize Governor Kathy Hochul's Housing Acceleration Fund. The project features two six-story buildings with retail and public park space; 30 units are designated affordable. Financing closed in July with $120.6 million construction debt from Merchants Capital, $10 million from Community Preservation Corporation, $18 million state financing, and $29.7 million equity from Basis Investment Group and BRP Companies; delivery expected Q2 2029.
stories.impact: NY State Housing Acceleration Fund removes regulatory and financing friction for mixed-income transit-oriented projects; signals state-level appetite to accelerate shovel-ready starts. White Plains' success as pilot will likely unlock similar entitlements and favorable financing terms for competing developers in lower-density Westchester and Hudson Valley markets, creating window to acquire sites and underwrite before supply inflects and cap rates compress.

stories.title: PMG Secures $250M Refi for New Fort Lauderdale Rental
stories.excerpt: Development firm PMG and private equity firm Greybook have secured $250 million to refinance a new multifamily building in Downtown Fort Lauderdale, property records show. The financing from Franklin Templeton’s Benefit Street Partners covers the second phase of the Society Las Olas complex, which was completed this year. The 42-story tower features 563 apartments at 140 Southwest Second Street and 219 Southwest First Avenue, between the New River and West Broward Boulevard. The debt replaces a $226 million construction loan issued in 2022 by Related Fund Management and Lubert-Adler, according to a representative for PMG. The joint venture completed Society Las Olas’ first phase — a neighboring 34-story, 639-unit building — in 2020. Two years later, it sold the property to Adam Neumann, the founder and former CEO of WeWork, for an undisclosed amount. He now operates the asset through his Flow housing venture. The new financing comes seven months after Flow purchased a 50 percent stake in PMG and Greybook’s Society multifamily property in Miami’s Wynwood neighborhood, The Real Deal reported. The 10-story building, completed in 2024, features 318 units. In recent months, PMG has focused on condo development, launching sales this year for the Delano condo development as well as the condo development branded by the hospitality firm co-founded by Kygo, a chart-topping Norwegian DJ. It has also secured construction financing for three condo projects in Miami. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: PMG and Greybook refinance Society Las Olas Phase 2, Fort Lauderdale: $250M, 42-story, 563 units.
Benefit Street Partners (Franklin Templeton) provided debt; replaced $226M 2022 construction loan.
Adam Neumann's Flow purchased 50% stake in PMG's multifamily portfolio July 2026; Phase 1 (639 units) sold to Flow in 2022.
stories.summary: PMG Development and Greybook secured $250 million in refinancing from Franklin Templeton's Benefit Street Partners for Society Las Olas Phase 2 in Downtown Fort Lauderdale, a completed 42-story tower with 563 apartments. The debt replaced a $226 million construction loan from Related Fund Management and Lubert-Adler. Adam Neumann's Flow housing venture acquired a 50% stake in PMG and Greybook's multifamily portfolio in July 2026 and previously purchased Phase 1 (639 units) in 2022.
stories.impact: Flow's continued capital deployment and stake-building in PMG's multifamily platform signals institutional conviction in South Florida rental demand and development expertise; refinancing at scale ($250M on completed asset) indicates strong property performance, supportive debt market for new supply, and capacity for developer to recycle equity into next-phase development. Downtown Fort Lauderdale's ability to support two phases of high-rise multifamily reflects sustained in-migration and white-collar job growth in Southeast Florida, supporting case for further development in Fort Lauderdale/Miami core.

stories.title: New Music Venue Signs Lease at Refinery at Domino
stories.excerpt: Two Trees Management has signed an entertainment tenant at the Refinery at Domino on the Williamsburg, Brooklyn, waterfront. London-based tvg Hospitality, which was founded by Mumford & Sons keyboardist Ben Lovett, and Emerson Hospitality signed the 20,000-square-foot lease for what will be a 750-seat venue called Domino, according to Two Trees. Two Trees did not disclose the asking rent or the length of the lease for the space at 20 River Street in Williamsburg, but the average asking rent for office space at the Refinery was $68 to $86 per square foot as of late October. “The neighborhood has changed enormously since [20 years ago], but for decades people have sought and found community in places like the one we’re building,” Lovett said in a statement. “Domino is our chance to carry that on: somewhere artists can develop ideas, audiences can discover something new, and neighbors feel they belong. Neighborhoods change. The need for a place like this never does.” There were no brokers involved in the deal, which will give Domino 10,000 square feet above ground and another 10,000 square feet below grade, according to Two Trees. “Williamsburg has an extraordinary and diverse cultural history of its own, and we’ve always believed that arts, music and creative spaces are essential to what makes the neighborhood interesting and vibrant,” Two Trees CEO Jed Walentas said in a statement. “Bringing live music and cultural programming to the ground floor of this historic building is a natural next chapter for the Refinery and will add a new dimension to the cultural life of the neighborhood.” The new venue is expected to open in April 2027. Crain’s New York Business first reported the lease. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Two Trees Management signs tvg Hospitality (Ben Lovett, Mumford & Sons) at Refinery at Domino, Williamsburg.
20,000 sq ft, 750-seat music venue; office asking rents $68–$86/sf as of late October.
Refinery at Domino is waterfront mixed-use redevelopment at 20 River Street, Brooklyn.
stories.summary: Two Trees Management leased 20,000 square feet at the Refinery at Domino in Williamsburg, Brooklyn, to tvg Hospitality and Emerson Hospitality for a 750-seat music venue called Domino. The venue is backed by Ben Lovett, keyboardist for Mumford & Sons. Office asking rents at the Refinery averaged $68–$86 per square foot as of late October; no broker was involved in the transaction.
stories.impact: Minimal relevance to multifamily development. Entertainment and hospitality tenancy at mixed-use waterfront development signals continued cultural vitality and foot traffic in Williamsburg, which can support adjacent rental housing demand, but the lease itself is office/entertainment, not residential. The deal suggests the Refinery's value-add strategy and leasing momentum support the broader asset's mixed-use thesis.

stories.title: DLC, Cohen & Steers Acquire Open-Air New Hampshire Center in Off-Market Deal
stories.excerpt: DLC, an owner and operator of open-air shopping centers, has completed the off-market acquisition of West Street Shopping Center, a 206,319-square-foot grocery-anchored shopping center in Keene, NH, in a joint venture with Cohen & Steers through its Cohen & Steers Real Estate Opportunities Fund. The sale price was not disclosed. West Street features the country’s No. 2-performing Hannaford and Hobby Lobby as anchors. Hannaford has operated there since 1984. “Our investment strategy is built on identifying opportunities where our experience gives us a competitive advantage,” said Adam Ifshin, founder and CEO of DLC. “We know this market, understand the fundamentals, and see significant upside in this asset. This is the kind of off-market opportunity where our knowledge and operating capabilities will drive meaningful long-term value.” Cohen & Steers said the acquisition aligns with its investment thesis of acquiring income-generating shopping centers anchored by necessity-based retailers in established markets with limited competitive retail supply. The post DLC, Cohen & Steers Acquire Open-Air New Hampshire Center in Off-Market Deal appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: DLC and Cohen & Steers acquire West Street Shopping Center, Keene, NH off-market for undisclosed price.
206,319 sq ft, grocery-anchored: Hannaford (No. 2 national performer, on-site since 1984) and Hobby Lobby.
Acquisition aligns with Cohen & Steers' thesis of necessity-based retail in established markets with limited competitive supply.
stories.summary: DLC and Cohen & Steers (through its Real Estate Opportunities Fund) completed an off-market acquisition of West Street Shopping Center in Keene, New Hampshire, a 206,319-square-foot grocery-anchored center featuring Hannaford and Hobby Lobby. Hannaford is the country's No. 2-performing location and has operated at the site since 1984. Purchase price was not disclosed.
stories.impact: No direct relevance to multifamily development. Acquisition of necessity-anchored retail in secondary markets reflects capital flight to grocery-anchored stability and lower-competition submarkets; does not signal residential demand or supply dynamics that would affect multifamily underwriting in Keene or surrounding region.

stories.title: CSC Real Estate In Contract to Buy Episcopal Church’s Manhattan HQ
stories.excerpt: CSC Real Estate, a New York-based investment firm specializing in residential conversions, is in contract to buy the Episcopal Church’s decades-old Manhattan headquarters. A spokesperson for CSC confirmed the pending transaction at 815 Second Avenue, known as the Episcopal Church Center, although the financial terms and the developer’s plans for the site were not disclosed. The Real Deal first reported news of the in-contract deal. In June, church leaders began testing the waters for a sale of the property, located at the corner of Second Avenue and East 43rd Street. The landlord tapped Denham Wolf Real Estate Services to market the 12-story building. A spokesperson for Denham declined to comment on the deal. The building’s current status as a largely vacant office building makes it a prime candidate for CSC’s portfolio of office-to-residential conversion projects. The developers recently secured financing to reposition a Midtown East office property at 136 East 57th Street into luxury apartments, CO reported in October, and in April secured a construction loan for an office-to-residential conversion at 770 Second Avenue in Murray Hill. A Lower Manhattan conversion at CSC’s 75 Maiden Lane and 13 Gold Street assemblage, acquired for $45.2 million in October 2025, is ongoing. The Episcopal Church has called 815 Second Avenue home since the building’s completion in the 1960s, according to The Washington Post. Church leadership began contemplating its sale in 2012, citing plans to relocate their HQ. Post-pandemic remote work policies have left the building largely vacant. “We occupy a fraction of the Church Center space now, and the conclusion is that we don’t need to own and occupy a building in Midtown Manhattan,” Chris Lacovara, the church’s chief financial officer, said in a recent statement. bullets: CSC Real Estate in contract to purchase Episcopal Church Center, Manhattan, 815 Second Avenue.
12-story largely vacant office building; prime conversion candidate for CSC's residential conversion portfolio.

stories.summary: CSC Real Estate, a New York-based firm specializing in residential conversions, is in contract to acquire the Episcopal Church Center at 815 Second Avenue (corner of Second Avenue and East 43rd Street) in Manhattan. The 12-story largely vacant office building is a prime candidate for conversion to residential use. CSC recently financed a luxury apartment conversion at 136 East 57th Street in Midtown East. Financial terms and specific development plans for 815 Second Avenue were not disclosed.
stories.impact: Manhattan office-to-residential conversion pipeline continues to absorb vacant Class B office stock in Midtown East, a submarket with significant vacancy and limited new office demand. CSC's deal-flow and financing access signal ongoing conversion feasibility at $PSF development costs below ground-up, supporting yield on repositioned assets. This activity reduces excess office supply but does not represent new net residential supply creation—it cannibalizes office inventory. Conversion velocity in Midtown East should be monitored; if absorption accelerates, ground-up multifamily development economics in adjacent submarkets (Kips Bay, Turtle Bay) may weaken as converted units absorb demand.

stories.title: Advanced Real Estate Buys Inland Empire Apartment Complex for $56M
stories.excerpt: Advanced Real Estate has expanded its multifamily portfolio after acquiring a 253-unit apartment community in Southern California’s Inland Empire for $56.2 million. The Orange County-based investment firm acquired Casitas Apartment Homes at 1900 South Campus Avenue in Ontario, Calif., for approximately $222,000 per unit, according to the Mogharebi Group, which arranged the sale. The advisory firm did not disclose the name of the private Los Angeles-based seller, but property records show Benedict Canyon Equities owned the property. Built in 1963, Casitas spans nearly 15 acres and features single-story buildings with one-bedroom apartments averaging 550 square feet and two-bedroom apartments averaging 775 square feet. The property is about four miles from Ontario International Airport. Advanced Real Estate assumed the property’s existing loan, which carries an interest rate of 3.11 percent. The loan balance and lender were not disclosed. “We were able to trade into this property with the equity from 13 smaller assets that were brought into (Advanced’s X Fund, via 721 contributions) in 2023,” Paul Julian, president of Advanced Real Estate, said in a statement. “Those contributing partners now have interest in this institutional-size asset which will yield much higher returns than their contributed smaller properties.” Otto Ozen and Jordan Pakzad of the Mogharebi Group represented the seller. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Advanced Real Estate acquires Casitas Apartment Homes, Ontario, CA (Inland Empire): 253 units, $56.2M ($222K/unit).
Built 1963, single-story buildings; assumed existing loan at 3.11% rate.
Property 4 miles from Ontario International Airport; seller was Benedict Canyon Equities.
stories.summary: Advanced Real Estate acquired Casitas Apartment Homes in Ontario, California, for $56.2 million (approximately $222,000 per unit), purchasing a 253-unit community built in 1963 across nearly 15 acres. The property features single-story buildings with one- and two-bedroom units and is located approximately four miles from Ontario International Airport. Advanced Real Estate assumed the property's existing loan at a 3.11 percent interest rate.
stories.impact: Sub-$225K per-unit acquisition price in Inland Empire signals value-add or distress transaction; assumed 3.11% loan is significantly below market, suggesting either legacy debt, assumable financing with lender consent, or seller carry. Low basis and favorable rate provide opportunity for cash-flowing hold or light repositioning. Inland Empire's proximity to Ontario Airport and logistics hubs continues to attract population and logistics employment; however, low per-unit price suggests building quality or unit mix challenges (1963 vintage, single-story), not macro demand weakness. Advanced Real Estate's acquisition strategy reflects Inland Empire's status as affordable, rent-growth market relative to coastal metros.

bullets: Altrio CEO Raj Singh discusses AI adoption necessity for CRE firms on Commercial Observer webinar.
Theme: AI shifts CRE professional role from execution to direction; intelligence and bandwidth constraints loosening.
Article frames AI as competitive necessity for workflows and decision-making across CRE services industry.
stories.summary: Raj Singh, CEO of tech provider Altrio, discussed on a November 10 Commercial Observer webinar the critical importance of AI adoption for commercial real estate firms. Singh emphasized that AI directly targets the value-creation core of CRE—information processing and decision-making by people—and that AI adoption shifts professional roles from task execution to orchestration. As intelligence becomes abundant and cheap, CRE professionals' competitive edge will depend on directing AI-driven workflows rather than performing manual work.
stories.impact: No direct impact on multifamily capital, supply, demand, or cost dynamics. Article is technology/operational commentary, not market signal. Indirect relevance only if AI adoption accelerates underwriting speed or reduces diligence costs for development teams, but this is marginal and affects all market participants equally.
